title: Aphrodite — Gods, heroes, and monsters
summary: Aphrodite, goddess of love and beauty, was born from sea foam according to Hesiod. This study profiles the figures at the myth's heart.
body:
Aphrodite, goddess of love and beauty, was born from sea foam according to Hesiod. Her judgment of Paris sparked the Trojan War.

Myths are carried by persons — gods who are larger than human, heroes who are almost, monsters who embody what must be faced. In Aphrodite, each figure plays a role that reveals what the culture feared, honored, and desired. Viewed through a contemporary-relevance lens, Aphrodite is brought into the present, where its patterns still appear in new clothes.

The figures of Aphrodite outlive their religion: they become metaphors the whole world now uses. One fruitful sub-question is which telling of Aphrodite is oldest, and how the tale changed in transmission. Related entries in this archive: Tanabata and Hanuman.
